beats.title: Lesson 13 — Detecting the Write Flood
beats.sub: The IDS catches a cyber-physical attack
beats.say: Welcome back to CybICS. In lesson six we seized control of the plant by flooding a Modbus register. That attack is loud. In this lesson we watch the intrusion detection system catch it.

beats.head: A flood is a signature
beats.body:
Overwriting a process value means writing the same register hundreds of times a second. Normal control traffic never looks like that.
  • The IDS counts Modbus writes per source in a sliding window.
  • More than fifty writes in five seconds trips the modbus_flood rule.
  • It maps to MITRE ATT&CK for ICS T0836, Modify Parameter.
beats.say: Overwriting a live process value means writing the same register hundreds of times a second. Normal control traffic never looks like that. The intrusion detection system counts Modbus writes per source in a sliding window, and more than fifty writes in five seconds trips its flood rule. This maps to MITRE technique T zero eight three six, modify parameter.

beats.caption: Replay the write flood from lesson 6
beats.say: We replay the attack from lesson six: the flood script hammers the high pressure tank register on the OpenP L C, thousands of writes in a few seconds. To the process it is an attempt to seize control. To the detector it is an unmistakable burst.

beats.caption: The defender's view: the IDS flags the flood
beats.say: Now the defender's view. We read the intrusion detection system's alert buffer, and the flood is right there: a Modbus flood alert, high severity, with our attack machine as the source. The attempt to seize the process was caught the moment it began.

beats.head: Detection buys time to respond
beats.body:
• A high-severity alert names the source and the rule the instant the flood starts.
  • An operator can isolate the source or fail the process to a safe state before pressure becomes critical.
Detection does not stop the write — but it turns a silent cyber-physical attack into an alarm a human can act on.
beats.say: A high severity alert names the source and the rule the instant the flood starts. With that, an operator can isolate the attacking host, or bring the process to a safe state, before the pressure becomes critical. Detection does not stop the write by itself, but it turns a silent cyber to physical attack into an alarm a human can act on.

beats.caption: Submit the flag in the CybICS dashboard - on the attack machine
beats.say: We finish on the dashboard, opening the detect the flood challenge and submitting the flag the intrusion detection system earns us for catching the write flood.

beats.head: What we learned
beats.body:
• A write flood is a clear signature — rapid writes to one register.
  • Monitor Modbus write rates per source and alert on bursts.
  • Pair detection with a safe-state response, so an alarm can protect the process, not just record the attack.
beats.say: To recap: a write flood is a clear signature, rapid writes to one register from one source. Monitor Modbus write rates and alert on bursts, and pair that detection with a safe state response, so the alarm protects the process rather than just recording the attack.
